info.title: Quarter
info.summary: The gateway and ledger that decide and record what AI agents spend.
info.description:
Quarter's own HTTP API, as served by `quarter-ledger serve` (proxy.py).

Agents call vendors through `/{vendor}/{path}` and ask before paying on any rail with `POST /authorize`, then report with `POST /settle`. People read reports and decide approvals with their own key and role (viewer, approver, finance, admin; each may do all that the ones before it may). Amounts in responses are micro-dollars unless a field says `_usd`.

Errors are JSON error objects carrying a message; their exact shape is not part of this description. Every response may carry the x-quarter-* headers listed under components.headers where they apply.

On every route: a body sent with `transfer-encoding` instead of `content-length` is answered 411; a bad length 400; a body over 8 MiB 413; a body over 64 KiB from a caller with no valid key 401. Ten wrong person keys from one address in five minutes lock it out (429) for the rest of that window.

Under a Quarter route's first segment, a method the route does not answer gets 405 with an `Allow` header (components/responses/E405), and a path that is no route gets 404; neither reaches a vendor.

post.summary: Authorise a payment before making it
post.description: The decision API that x402 clients and other rail adapters call. Quarter applies caps, approval limits, pauses, payee lists, the feed's payee flags and sanctions screening, holds the amount, and answers with a signed authorisation valid for `expires_in` seconds. No money passes through Quarter. With `x-quarter-wait` a payment that needs approval waits for the decision instead of answering 403 at once; approved while waiting, it is authorised. Retry a payment that needed approval with `x-quarter-approval`. Counted as a decision against QUARTER_FREE_DECISIONS.

payee.description: Who is paid, e.g. an 0x address.

amount_usd.description: US dollars, for example "0.25". Used when amount_micros is absent.

amount_micros.description: Micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000). Takes precedence over amount_usd.

network.description: The x402 network, for the feed's price check.

resource.description: The URL paid for, for the feed's price check.

schema.description: One of amount_micros or amount_usd is required; positive, at most $1 billion.

authorisation.description: A signed token (JWT) naming the agent, rail, payee and max_amount_micros.

authorization.description: The same token as authorisation, under the US spelling of the path. authorisation stays for clients that read it.

shadow.description: Present when a rule in shadow mode would have held it.

mandate.description: A spend mandate for the seller, when QUARTER_ORG is set and the signing key is ed25519. Sent in the x402 payment as the company-policy extension.

400.description: Bad JSON, an unknown rail, no payee, a non-positive amount, an amount over $1 billion, or a bad x-quarter-wait.

401.description: An agent key is configured and none was sent.

402.description: Over a cap. Retrying will not help until the window resets or the cap changes.

403.description: Refused: the payee is not allowed, a sanctions match, the approval was denied, the agent key belongs to another agent, or an approval is required (the body carries the approval id; retry with x-quarter-approval once a person approves).

423.description: The agent or the task is paused.

post.description: The hold made by /authorize becomes the real charge. Settling 0 releases it. Paying more than authorised is recorded and audited as over_authorised. With `x402_response` (the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header the agent got back) the transaction and network are read from it, and a failed payment settles at 0. Only the agent that authorised may settle.

get.description: Forwarded to the vendor's base URL (openai, anthropic, gemini, openrouter, chatgpt, or an upstream from the config). The vendor's API is not described here. A model call's worst-case cost is held first and settled to what it really cost; a call to an API that is not a model is not held, and is audited as upstream_call. PUT, PATCH and DELETE are only ever forwarded. The agent key may also arrive where the vendor key goes (Authorization: Bearer, or x-api-key), and is then swapped for the vendor's key; otherwise the vendor's own key travels with the request.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The rest of the vendor's path, slashes included.

2XX.description: The vendor's reply, relayed as it came (streams as they arrive), with Quarter's headers added. A reply holding a tool call a rule holds has that call replaced by a note until a person approves.

400.description: A bad path, a body that is not JSON, a bad x-quarter-wait, or a model with no price anywhere.

401.description: An agent key is configured and none was sent.

402.description: Over a cap. The call did not reach the vendor.

403.description: Refused before the vendor: a rule denies it, the approval was denied, the agent key belongs to another agent, or an approval is required (the body carries the approval id; retry with x-quarter-approval).

423.description: The agent or the task is paused.

502.description: The vendor was unreachable, or the connection was lost after sending (charged, never resent).

503.description: The gateway has no key for that vendor, or the ledger is unavailable.

default.description: Any other vendor status, relayed with Quarter's headers.

agent.name: x-quarter-agent
agent.description: The agent. Else the name given to the agent key, else "default". A named key may speak only for its agent (403).

task.name: x-quarter-task
task.description: The task. Claude Code's x-claude-code-session-id is the default.

customer.name: x-quarter-customer
customer.description: The customer the spend is for.

approval.name: x-quarter-approval
approval.description: An approved approval id, to retry a call or payment that needed approval.

wait.name: x-quarter-wait
wait.description: Seconds to hold a call or payment that needs approval open until someone decides; at most 300, or QUARTER_MAX_WAIT.

approver.name: x-quarter-approver
approver.description: Who is deciding. Must match the person signed in, unless the shared admin key is used (403 otherwise).

cache.name: x-quarter-cache
cache.description: "off" stops Quarter adding Anthropic's cache marker.

fallback.name: x-quarter-fallback
fallback.description: "off" stops Quarter moving the call to a cheaper model near a cap.

month.name: month
month.description: YYYY-MM, not later than this month. In the first 7 days of a month the default is last month.

x-quarter-call.description: The call's id in the ledger.

x-quarter-shadow.description: Let through only because a rule is in shadow mode: what it would have done.

x-quarter-free-limit.description: Past QUARTER_FREE_DECISIONS this month; the call is decided as ever.

x-quarter-upstream.description: A routing rule sent the call to this upstream instead.

x-quarter-redacted.description: What was masked before the model saw it, and put back in the reply.

x-quarter-billing.description: Paid by a plan, recorded at no cost.

x-quarter-model.description: Moved to a cheaper model near a cap: "asked -> used".

x-quarter-fail-open.description: The ledger could not be written and QUARTER_FAIL_OPEN let this model call through.

agentKey.name: x-quarter-key
agentKey.description: An agent key. Not needed when no agent keys are configured.

agentBearer.description: An agent key where the vendor key goes.

agentApiKey.name: x-api-key
agentApiKey.description: An agent key where Anthropic's key goes.

personKey.name: x-quarter-key
personKey.description: A person's key (QUARTER_PEOPLE) or QUARTER_ADMIN_KEY. The operation's x-quarter-role is the least role it needs.

personBasic.description: HTTP basic auth: the password is a person's key or the admin key; any username.

slackSignature.name: x-slack-signature
slackSignature.description: Slack's signature over x-slack-request-timestamp and the raw body, at most 5 minutes old.

stripeSignature.name: stripe-signature
stripeSignature.description: Stripe's webhook signature with the endpoint's whsec_ secret.

Error.description: An error object carrying a message, and sometimes more (such as an approval id).

status.description: approved, waiting, refused, paying, paid and so on.

E403.description: Cross-site request refused, or the person's role is below the one needed.

E403Role.description: The person's role is below the one needed.

E429.description: Too many wrong keys from this address; try again later.

BackToDashboard.description: From the dashboard's form: back to it.

E405.description: The path is a Quarter route, but not for this method.
